docs.question: How many bike stations are there?
docs.answer: There are 115 bike stations in the Dublin bike-share network.
docs.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS station_count FROM marts.dim_station LIMIT 200

docs.question: Which station is closest to O'Connell Bridge?
docs.answer: Princes Street / O'Connell Street is the closest station, about 0.22 km from O'Connell Bridge, with a capacity of 23 docks. The next nearest is Townsend Street at roughly 0.34 km.

docs.question: Which station has spent the most minutes empty?
docs.answer: GRANGEGORMAN LOWER (CENTRAL) has spent the most time empty, at about 407 minutes, ahead of JAMES STREET EAST (352) and HERBERT STREET (350).

docs.question: Which 3 stations have the highest peak-hour shortage rate?
docs.answer: The three stations with the highest peak-hour shortage rate are PHIBSBOROUGH ROAD (inner zone) at 100.0%, GOLDEN LANE (city centre) at 70.7%, and PORTOBELLO ROAD (inner) at 59.9%.

docs.question: Compare the average number of available bikes in hours with precipitation versus dry hours.
docs.answer: Across the observed station-hours, the availability-weighted average was 11.83 bikes in dry hours (45,683 observed minutes) versus 11.61 bikes in hours with precipitation (21,364 observed minutes) — a drop of about 0.2 bikes. Per station, the average rain-vs-dry difference is -0.35 bikes across 113 stations, though individual stations range widely from -25.9 to +26.3, so the effect is small on average and inconsistent between stations.
